source: Create a game based on ww2 in which the players can create their base and they have to attack other bases & defend their own base from other players. They have to save themselves from the developer's tank named as "Siger & nex"

image_prompt.text: Broad open buildable ground radiating out from each player base where players raise their own WWII fortifications, gated by proximity rather than a fixed grid

layout_placement.text: Each player base has a core structure standing for its health, defensible from every direction because no lane funnels attackers
Scattered supply sites players expand toward and fight over
Where the developer tank Siger and Nex enters the map and the ground it patrols between the bases

notes: tracker-core is a both option and so appears in the image stream as the visible base core as well.

The prompt never says whether players command units from above or fight as avatars on the ground. Strategy was chosen because the sentence is about building, attacking and defending bases, but if this is meant to be an on-foot WWII shooter the shape and the whole option set change.
The named developer tank was promoted to spawner-npc as a roaming hostile with an origin and patrol ground; nothing in the loaded file expresses a single scripted boss vehicle.

open_questions.ask: Do players see the battlefield from above and place units, or run around as soldiers?
How many bases share a map, and how far apart should they sit?

coverage_missing.ask: Is this commanded from a top-down view, or played on foot?
How many players and how many bases per server?
Does a round end when a base core falls, or does the world persist between sessions?
Which WWII front - European towns, desert, Pacific island?

answers.ask: Do players see the battlefield from above and place units, or run around as soldiers?
answers.answer: Players run around as soldiers in third-person, building and defending their own bases while attacking others.

answers.ask: How many bases share a map, and how far apart should they sit?
answers.answer: Use a small map with 4 player bases, placed far enough apart that each base has its own defensible area but can be reached on foot without a long journey.
